summary:
MISSIONFORGE: Interactive Space Mission Simulator

MISSIONFORGE is an interactive 3D web-based space mission design and simulation game developed for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. It allows players to explore the Solar System, design spacecraft, select propulsion systems and scientific instruments, manage fuel, power, mass and budgets, and plan missions to different planetary destinations.

The project addresses the challenge by transforming complex space mission planning into an engaging, educational experience. Players make engineering decisions, simulate mission stages, respond to unexpected challenges, and evaluate their mission performance through scientific objectives and resource management.

MISSIONFORGE aims to make space exploration and aerospace engineering more accessible by helping users understand the science, technology and teamwork behind real space missions. By combining interactive 3D visualisation, simplified physics and game-based learning, it encourages curiosity, critical thinking and interest in space science and engineering.
details:
MISSIONFORGE — Educational Space Mission Design & Simulation Game

https://missionforge.qorvode.co.in/

What It Does & How It Works

MISSIONFORGE is an interactive, browser-based space mission design and simulation platform where players step into the roles of Spacecraft Mission Engineer and Mission Director to design, configure, launch, and operate robotic exploration missions across the Solar System.

Rather than simply selecting a destination and clicking launch, players manage end-to-end aerospace trade-offs across nine flight phases:

1. Explore & Plan: Navigate a 3D Solar System to inspect planetary telemetry, select a destination, define scientific objectives, and set mission duration and budgets.

2. Build the Spacecraft: Assemble a modular 3D spacecraft—configuring the structural bus, solar arrays or RTGs, high-gain antennas, propulsion systems, propellant tanks, and scientific instruments—while watching mass, power, thermal, and cost metrics update in real time.

3. Select Launch & Trajectory: Match the spacecraft's wet mass to an appropriate launch vehicle (such as Falcon 9, Falcon Heavy, SLS, Atlas V, Ariane 6, Starship, or Electron) and plan interplanetary Hohmann transfer windows and delta-v budgets.

4. Launch & Operate: Execute a nine-phase mission from pre-launch countdown and orbital insertion through interplanetary cruise, mid-course corrections, arrival capture burns, and scientific operations.

5. Handle Dynamic Anomalies: Respond under pressure to real-time engineering events—such as solar particle events, micrometeoroid impacts, communication blackouts, thermal extremes, and sensor glitches—by making calculated operational trade-offs.

6. Mission Debrief: Receive a weighted post-flight evaluation across five pillars—Scientific Objectives (30%), Engineering Performance (25%), Mission Completion (20%), Budget Efficiency (15%), and Resource Management (10%)—with exportable JSON and printable mission reports.

Benefits & Intended Impact

- Bridges Theory and Intuition: Transforms abstract orbital mechanics and systems engineering formulas into hands-on, cause-and-effect decision-making where every kilogram, watt, and dollar has a direct impact on mission survival.

- Accessible STEM Education: Runs completely in the browser as an offline-first application with zero installation or heavy hardware requirements, making authentic space mission engineering accessible to students, educators, and space enthusiasts anywhere.

Tools, Coding Languages & Software Used

- Core Framework & Languages: React 19, TypeScript (Strict mode), and Vite.

- 3D Graphics & Visualization: Three.js, React Three Fiber, @react-three/drei, procedural HTML5 Canvas planetary textures, and Recharts for real-time telemetry graphs.

- State, Styling & Testing: Zustand (with localStorage persistence), Tailwind CSS v4, Framer Motion, Lucide React, and Vitest for deterministic physics verification.

- Data Sources: Adapted from public NASA Goddard Space Flight Center (GSFC) Planetary Fact Sheets, NASA Launch Services Program (LSP) performance curves, and deep-space mission heritage (Voyager, Cassini-Huygens, New Horizons, Perseverance, Europa Clipper, and Parker Solar Probe).

How Our Project Is Creative

- Authentic SI-Unit Physics Inside Interactive Gameplay: Instead of arbitrary game stats, MISSIONFORGE runs a deterministic, fixed-step engineering engine modeled on real physics—including coplanar Keplerian orbits, the vis-viva equation, the Tsiolkovsky rocket equation (with a 12% structural mass margin), inverse-square solar irradiance (1361 W/m² at 1 AU), Stefan-Boltzmann radiative thermal equilibrium, and speed-of-light deep-space signal delays.

- Procedural & Offline-First Architecture: All planetary surfaces, starfields, and spacecraft assemblies are procedurally generated on the client side with zero runtime CDN dependencies, ensuring smooth performance and full offline capability.

Factors Our Team Considered

- Realism vs. Accessibility: We balanced authentic aerospace constraints (delta-v budgets, duty cycles, thermal sink limits, and downlink path loss) with intuitive visual feedback and simplified two-impulse transfer classes so newcomers can grasp orbital mechanics without needing an aerospace degree.

- Client-Side Reliability: Designed as a zero-backend static Single Page Application with hash routing and deterministic seeded RNG so users can save mission archives locally and run repeatable simulations on standard laptops.
